prs.title: fix(linter/vitest/prefer-to-be-truthy): suggest assertion rewrites
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Reclassify `vitest/prefer-to-be-truthy`, `vitest/prefer-to-be-falsy`, and Jest/Vitest `prefer-strict-equal` replacements as suggestions, since they change which values pass an assertion. Plain `--fix` now preserves these assertions; `--fix-suggestions` applies the replacements.

Add regression coverage for both fix modes and clarify the truthy/falsy rule documentation.

Fixes #26760

prs.title: fix(linter/eslint/preserve-caught-error): prevent conflicting fixes with prefer-optional-catch-binding
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Include an unchanged catch-binding replacement in each `preserve-caught-error` fix so it overlaps with fixes that remove the binding. With `unicorn/prefer-optional-catch-binding` enabled, `catch (error) { throw new Error('message'); }` now becomes `catch { throw new Error('message'); }` instead of adding a dangling `cause: error` reference.

Fixes for multiple throws sharing a catch binding now overlap and apply one per pass. Regression tests cover the conflicting fix paths and fixing a remaining throw on a later pass.

Fixes #26682.

fix(transformer): skip enum reverse mappings for syntactic string initializers
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
A member whose value is a string never gets a reverse mapping, but the enum lowering decides that with `is_string_literal()`, so any string-valued initializer the constant evaluator cannot fold is lowered like a number. The inner assignment then produces a string, and the outer write adds a bogus key that can overwrite a real member: with `const foo = "x"`, an enum containing `"xa" = 1` and `A = foo + "a"` ends up with `E["xa"] === "A"` instead of `1`.

Decide syntactically, the way tsc does in `isSyntacticallyString`: string literals, template literals, and additions with a string on either side are strings, looking through parentheses only. An `as`, `satisfies`, non-null, or angle bracket assertion around a string is not syntactically a string, so `("x" as string)` keeps its reverse mapping. Anything else, including `typeof x` and `1 + foo`, keeps its reverse mapping too, matching tsc's emit exactly.

Noticed while auditing enum lowering for #26242; the mis-lowering predates that work and affects plain code, so it targets main directly. The lone-surrogate connection is indirect: on main this path is not reached for `"\uD800" + "\uDC00"`, because the constant evaluator still folds it through the marker encoding. The JSStr migration makes the evaluator decline such strings, and the initializer then falls through to this classifier. With this rule it lowers as a string, so it cannot overwrite a sibling member named by the pair's value. A regression test for that case follows o
…(truncated)

fix(linter/esliny/no-unused-vars): preserve rest bindings when removing array elements
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Removing an unused element immediately before an array rest binding treated it as the final element and deleted both surrounding commas, producing invalid syntax such as `[used...rest]`.

Keep the element’s placeholder when a rest binding follows, producing `[used, ,...rest]` so the rest binding retains the same values. Adds a regression test for the suggested fix.

prs.title: fix(linter/esliny/no-unused-vars): handle comments when removing imports
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Removing an unused named import stopped at a comment before the separator, leaving invalid syntax such as `import {/* comment */, used} from "m"`.

Find the separator token across comments and remove it separately from the unused specifier, preserving the comment. Adds regression coverage for block comments, line comments, and commas inside comments.

prs.title: fix(formatter_markdown): fix real-world missmatches
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
1. Code span fences: Line-start detection should look at printed (=recalculated) fence rather than the source text
2. Leading `---` paragraphs: Dropping leading blank lines would turn the next line into front matter, so escape to `\---`
3. `---<div>` closing lines: The printer slices the same painted copy as the parser, prevent duplicating `---`
4. Autolink + CJK: After words within an autolink literal stretch, follow CJK rules by inserting a space instead of removing line breaks to preserve link
5. Line shape inside nests: Determines the shape even for line breaks within `emphasis` and other elements
6. Reference link wrapping: Wraps the `text` part of `[text][label]`
7. Liquid glue: With `always`, whitespace immediately following a tag is not wrapped (whitespace immediately preceding it was already prohibited)
8. Directive blank lines: Preserves blank lines between the `:::` fence and follows the same blank line behavior

prs.title: fix(linter/eslint/no-unused-vars): report private namespace bindings
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
A root export such as `export const value = 1` incorrectly suppresses the unused-variable diagnostic for a private `value` declared inside a TypeScript namespace.

Restrict the module-level export-name lookup to root symbols. Namespace bindings still use their own export declarations, so private unused bindings are reported even when a root export shares their name. Adds regression coverage for direct and aliased root exports, nested namespaces, and used or explicitly exported namespace bindings.

feat(oxlint,oxfmt): do not discover nested config in Vite+ mode
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
When Vite+ support was first added, whether to support nested config or not was undecided.
But for now, that policy has now been finalized, and it was decided to NOT support in v1.

Technically, Vite+ can disable nested configs by specifying either `-c` or `--disable-nested-config`.
However, this only applies to the CLI. For LSP usage, this needs to be applied to arbitrary workspace settings, but users can set any directory as a workspace. (Also we are trying to remove `-c`, #26755)

Therefore, as the SSoT consolidating Vite+ requirements, disable it on the Oxapps (`oxc_config`) side.

Doing this eliminates [the need for each IDE extension to implement the same forced disablement individually](https://github.com/voidzero-dev/vite-plus/issues/1557#issuecomment-5710627758), and makes it easier to revert changes even if the policy is modified.

As a bonus, this also prevents [performance issue](voidzero-dev/vite-plus#2698) caused by searching through unintended nested configs.

fix(linter/eslint/prefer-const): ignore embedded assignments
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Avoid reporting `prefer-const` when an uninitialized variable's only assignment is embedded in another expression, such as `let a; foo(a = 1)`. Like ESLint, require the assignment to be a standalone statement where a declaration is allowed, while allowing surrounding parentheses.

Adds the reported TypeScript example and regression cases for calls, initializers, returns, chained assignments, destructuring, and loop bodies.

Fixes #26913.

prs.title: fix(linter/eslint/no-unused-vars): recognize consumed update expressions
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
`no-unused-vars` incorrectly reports variables whose updated values are consumed, such as `let a = 0; new Foo(a++);`.

Recognize constructor arguments, computed member access, switch discriminants, and conditional/logical tests as uses of update values. Keep warnings for discarded updates and self-assignments, with regression coverage for both cases.

prs.title: fix(linter/eslint/no-unused-vars): honor ignore patterns inside array rest bindings
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
`no-unused-vars` reports `const [...[_rest]] = items` despite `destructuredArrayIgnorePattern: "^_"` because the binding-pattern search skips array rest arguments. Recurse into those arguments so nested arrays and objects respect `destructuredArrayIgnorePattern` and `ignoreRestSiblings`.

Includes regression coverage for declarations and parameters, with controls for plain rest identifiers and nonmatching names.

refactor(lexer): extract operator hashing into function
perf(lexer): convert opmap collision checks into test
fix(codegen): remove redundant dollar escapes in minified templates
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Remove redundant dollar escapes from untagged templates when minifying:

```js
// Before
`^${pattern}\$`
// After
`^${pattern}$`
```

Preserve escapes that prevent `${` interpolation and account for escaped backslashes. Tagged templates retain their raw spelling, and non-minified output keeps its existing behavior.

The normal minsize corpus shrinks by 11 raw bytes and 8 gzip bytes across Ant Design and TypeScript; Brotli grows by 2 bytes.

prs.title: fix(linter/unicorn/prefer-spread): stop checking string split calls
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Stop reporting and fixing `String#split('')`, matching Unicorn's removal of this check in v66. Splitting into UTF-16 code units and spreading into code points can produce different results, for example for `"🦄"`.

Fixes #26873

prs.title: fix(linter/import/no-duplicates): distinguish import attributes
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Treat imports with different attribute keys or values as distinct in `import/no-duplicates`, without adding an option. This follows the upstream maintainer's guidance in https://github.com/import-js/eslint-plugin-import/issues/3290#issuecomment-5771071222; the current upstream release (2.32.0) and main branch still have the same false positive.

Group imports by normalized attributes before applying the existing import-kind checks. Attribute order and quoted keys do not matter, and an empty attribute clause matches an absent clause. Regression tests cover the Bun macro example, custom attributes, genuine duplicates, and `prefer-inline` interactions.

Fixes #26871.

prs.title: fix(linter/node/no-exports-assign): change category from style to suspicious
prs.author: Bartok9
prs.body:
Closes #26282. `exports = {}` is most likely a bug (reassigns the local `exports` binding, not `module.exports`), so it fits the `suspicious` category better than `style`. Test still passes.

prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Split out from #26919 to reduce the size of the diff on that PR.

That PR requires `popcnt` CPU feature for SIMD implementation. Alter all `#[cfg(...)]` blocks to include `target_feature = "popcnt"`.

prs.title: fix(lexer): support HTML-like comments in JSX files
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Split off from #26919, to reduce the size of that PR's diff.

Annex B HTML-like comments (``) were only handled when lexing plain JS. In JSX files they were lexed as operators.

This moves the `` handling out of `carve_js` into shared helpers in `carve/common.rs`, and uses them in `carve_jsx` too. The rules are the same as for JS: in scripts both are comments, and in modules only a `` only starts a comment once a `` means stopping at every `>`, and JSX is full of them, so that's only switched on when needed.

prs.title: fix(lexer): handle comments and Unicode whitespace in JSX tags
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Split off from #26919, to reduce the size of that PR's diff.

Several places in JSX carve only expected ASCII whitespace (or nothing) between tokens, so a comment or Unicode whitespace (e.g. NBSP) there threw it off:

- Closing and self-closing tags: `</*c*//a>`, `<\u{a0}/a>`, `</a\u{a0}>`, `<a / /*c*/ >`. Comments in these spots are now lexed as comments rather than operators.
- Member tag names: `<A/*c*/.B>x</A.B>` no longer reports a mismatched closing tag.
- Between `<` and the tag name: Unicode whitespace is now skipped. Comments already were.
- In `.tsx`, the look-ahead that tells a type parameter list from a JSX element: `<T /*c*/ extends U>`, `<T //c\n,>`, `<const /*c*/ T>`, and `let f: <T> /*c*/ (x: T) => T;`, which was lexed as a JSX element.

Also, the `const` modifier in `<const T>` now has to be on the same line as its parameter, as in TypeScript.

prs.author: Boshen
prs.body:
## Summary

- add threadless `wasm32-wasip1` builds and generated loaders for parser, minify, transform, transform-react, and transform-relay
- use the threadless bindings for browser and Cloudflare Workers while preserving threaded WASI and WebContainer fallbacks
- build and publish the new target in CI and release workflows

Closes #25271

## Testing

- native NAPI builds and package tests: 1,091 passed
- parser Chromium browser tests passed
- local workerd smoke tests passed for all five packages
- deployed Workers using local package tarballs passed for all five packages and reported `wasm32-wasip1`
- packed main-package file lists match the published `0.150.0` packages
- `just fmt`, `just check`, `just lint`, `just doc`, `just ast`, targeted Oxlint, typos, and `git diff --check` passed
- `just ready` reaches three unrelated Oxlint ANSI-color snapshot mismatches in this non-interactive environment; no pending snapshots remain

## AI assistance

Codex was used to help implement and test this change. The contributor remains responsible for reviewing and understanding the changes before merge.
